messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Stan in R 3.0
parts:
Hi all. Just for laffs I tried installing Stan in the new R. It worked. But I did get the following warnings near the beginning:

> ## add current repository of rstan
> options(repos = c(getOption("repos"), rstan = "http://wiki.stan.googlecode.com/git/R"))
> install.packages('rstan', type = 'source')
'.path.package' is deprecated.
Use 'path.package' instead.
See help("Deprecated")
Warning in install.packages :
cannot open: HTTP status was '404 Not Found'
Warning in install.packages :
cannot open: HTTP status was '404 Not Found'
Warning in install.packages :
unable to access index for repository http://wiki.stan.googlecode.com/git/R/bin/macosx/contrib/3.0
Warning in install.packages :
package ‘rstan’ is not available (for R version 3.0.0)


I also needed to re-edit the Makeconf file with the new R, it might be worth reminding people they need to do that.

A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan in R 3.0
parts:
On 4/4/13 2:11 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> Hi all. Just for laffs I tried installing Stan in the new R. It worked. But I did get the following warnings near the beginning:

Now that R 3.0.0 is official, we should definitely make the
install a bit more seamless.

>> ## add current repository of rstan
>> options(repos = c(getOption("repos"), rstan = "http://wiki.stan.googlecode.com/git/R"))
>> install.packages('rstan', type = 'source')
> '.path.package' is deprecated.
> Use 'path.package' instead.
> See help("Deprecated")

That's cryptic, but hopefully the R developers will know
what it means

> Warning in install.packages :
> cannot open: HTTP status was '404 Not Found'
> Warning in install.packages :
> cannot open: HTTP status was '404 Not Found'

These 404 warnings looks like the bug we reported for
RStudio.

> Warning in install.packages :
> unable to access index for repository http://wiki.stan.googlecode.com/git/R/bin/macosx/contrib/3.0

Looks like we need to create that.

> Warning in install.packages :
> package ï¿½rstanï¿½ is not available (for R version 3.0.0)

And it worked after this? I think they may just mean we're
not on CRAN?

Anyway, if we can't hack around the warnings, we need to at
least let users know they should expect them.
> I also needed to re-edit the Makeconf file with the new R, it might be worth reminding people they need to do that.

Good idea.

Thanks for giving it a whirl.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan in R 3.0
parts:
Thanks for testing R 3.0.  I think the problem is still with RStudio.  I do not have any problem with using plain R. 

Actually, I can even reproduce this this time. But I only have
> install.packages('rstan', type = 'source')

Warning in install.packages :
  cannot open: HTTP status was '404 Not Found'
Warning in install.packages :
  cannot open: HTTP status was '404 Not Found'

Warning in install.packages :
  unable to access index for repository http://wiki.stan.googlecode.com/git/R/bin/macosx/contrib/3.0

Warning in install.packages :
  package ‘rstan’ is not available (for R version 3.0.0)
trying URL 'http://wiki.stan.googlecode.com/git/R/src/contrib/rstan_1.2.0.tar.gz'
Content type 'application/x-gzip' length unknown
opened URL
.......... .......... .......... .......... ..........
.......... 

So the good news is still that in the end it finds the source that we provide and makes it.  

The error happens because it is trying to find a binary version of rstan, which we do not provide.  (This is not because we are not on CRAN and I can install rstan without this false warning using R from the command line.)

I added two empty index file for the binary packages to our google/rstan/wiki repo.  This can remove the 404 error, but I still have
> install.packages('rstan', type = 'source')

Warning in install.packages :
  package ‘rstan’ is not available (for R version 3.0.0)

..........

--
Jiqiang
